title: 1.5 · How much can you trust the number?

blocks.statement: I can choose an instrument suited to a task and explain the limits of repeated measurements.

blocks.markdown:
## The job sets the needed precision

A reading to the nearest 1/16 inch cannot support every job. Compare the smallest readable division with the stated tolerance, then consider calibration, setup and the object. Select a tool with enough resolution and verified performance for the task.

frames.text: My evidence is ___. This supports ___ because ___.
My conclusion is ___; my evidence is ___.

question.prompt: A supplied task requires checking a 0.01-inch difference. Which plan is best?

options.text: Use a tape marked every 1/16 inch and guess.
options.feedback: A 1/16-inch division is 0.0625 inch, coarser than this difference.

options.text: Use a checked instrument with resolution finer than 0.01 inch and repeat the measurement.
options.feedback: Yes. Resolution is necessary, and you still must check performance and setup.

options.text: Repeat the coarse tape reading ten times; that adds smaller divisions.
options.feedback: Repeating a measurement does not add physical scale divisions or remove systematic error.

steps: Choose one suitable object and record the tool’s smallest readable division.
Measure five times, lifting and replacing the tool each time.
Calculate highest minus lowest. Record all readings, including repeated ones.
Compare a second tool if available. State what each tool is useful for and what you cannot conclude.
